summary.intent: Complete Wave 0 of the frontend-design evaluation plan and build Wave 1 exploration modes (sketch, promote, spike skills, explorer agent, new schemas, ADR 011) in the wisp-plugins worktree, piloting each and logging honest status.
summary.outcome: Wave 0 second pass was logged and committed. Wave 1 was built: option-set@1 and spike-report@1 schemas, explorer agent, sketch/promote/spike skills with Codex counterparts, ADR 011, modes reference, README and manifest wiring, and new tests. Each skill was piloted with claude -p, and the findings were recorded. `just check` passes (103 tests). The Wave 1 commits had not yet been made.

repo: Codex skills under harnesses/codex are native sources checked by tests/test_codex_native_sources.py. Editing one without running `just marketplace-sync` fails the drift test, so always resync after changing them.

Codex only delegates when explicitly told, so Codex skills must use explicit 'start a subagent with this packet' wording. Role cards cannot enforce read-only because subagents inherit the parent sandbox.

Manifest and marketplace files are generated or synced via `just claude-manifests-sync` and `just marketplace-sync`. Codex plugin.json files use inline arrays, so a json.dump rewrite creates noisy diffs. Use targeted text edits instead.
New ADRs must also be added to the docs/adr/README.md index. tests/test_reference_integrity.py enforces this.
scripts/check-reference-size.sh warns on reference file word count, so modes.md had to be trimmed to fit.
shared/scripts/validate-wiring.sh reports one pre-existing warning about an external optional schema, unrelated to this work.
`claude plugin validate` takes a component directory (e.g. plugins/muse/skills), not a single file path. A single file is parsed as JSON.
Agents share a five-part structure with a byte-identical constitution and tiers, now enforced for all 45 agents by tests/test_agent_structure.py.
Final counts: 10 plugins, 33 skills, 45 agents, 33 schemas.

code.finding: Extended with `pattern` support, since the new schemas option-set@1 and spike-report@1 use regex patterns. Tested in tests/test_exploration_schemas.py.

workflow: Pilot new skills with `claude -p --plugin-dir ... --permission-mode auto --max-budget-usd N` in a clean /private/tmp directory, then validate the produced artifacts against the schemas.
Schema files were not reliably readable at run time in pilots. Inlining the record shape in each skill dropped schema violations from 22 to 0 on the same prompt.
Long compound shell commands were rejected by the command guard. Putting prompts in files and splitting run and inspect into separate commands worked.
`--permission-mode acceptEdits` plus `--allowedTools` did not suffice for the spike pilot. `--permission-mode auto` worked.
The Playwright browser blocks file: URLs, so a temporary localhost http.server was used to view the pilot output, then stopped and cleaned up.
Writing status tables with explicit Done/Partly/Not started and a 'Not yet done' column keeps implementation logs honest.

friction: Pilot runs from the .claude/jobs tmp directory behaved differently from a clean /private/tmp directory, so the pilot had to be rerun elsewhere.
The first pilot sketch record did not conform to option-set@1 (22 violations) because the schema file was not reliably read at run time.
The Codex manifest edit via JSON dump reformatted the files and had to be reverted with git checkout.
The Codex source edit triggered the drift test until the bundle was regenerated.
An earlier stray space ('implementation ; code-level') in a description needed fixing.
A preview board was clipped, which led to adding a board-frame tip to both skills.
open_items: The Wave 1 changes are uncommitted. The final step was `git status`, and the commits are meant to be split by topic.
ADR 011 was written as Accepted by the author and needs reviewer confirmation in the pull request.

Wave 0 still open: WP-109 defect-corpus fixtures, WP-440 instruction-file linter, wiring the analysis tool into mason:evaluate, the committed plugin-eval suite, and the isolated install test for WP-621/622.
Wave 1 not started: WP-19, WP-20, WP-21, WP-309.
Partly done: WP-12 (capability detection and a tested board generator), WP-13 (cross-session decision retrieval), WP-16 (anti-slop controls), WP-305/306 (automated divergence check).
WP-512 write guard is only an instruction, and a deterministic hook depends on WP-602.
A mode-router skill, the full spec@2 promote (Wave 3), the critique skill, and the muse recon and copy agents are not built.
Evaluation of sketch and spike against ad hoc exploration is not done.
The per-harness probe on Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Haiku 5.5 is not done, and the open decision on the Codex TOML generator (N8) remains.
